explanation: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain later turned penicillin into a usable medicine during the Second World War, and all three shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

claims.text: In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed that a Penicillium mould had killed nearby bacteria, the observation that led to penicillin.
Louis Pasteur, Joseph Lister and Robert Koch did not discover penicillin.
Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed penicillin into a usable medicine in the early 1940s, during the Second World War.
Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
